title: Mikor lehet?: Possibility and Opening Hours

sections.title: Possibility changes with time and place
sections.content: lehet + infinitive often depends on when or where you ask — the same activity can be possible in one place and not in another, or possible at one time and not another. Add a time or place expression in front, and combine it with mindig, néha, and soha, which you already know, to say how often something is possible.

sections.title: Time, place and frequency with lehet
rows: In the summer you can swim in the lake.
A könyvtárban mindig lehet csendben olvasni.
In the library you can always read quietly.
Este már nem lehet bemenni a múzeumba.
In the evening you can no longer get into the museum.

items.spanish: Milyen a nyitvatartás? Mikor lehet idejönni?
items.english: What are the opening hours? When can you come here?

items.spanish: Reggel lehet a parkban futni, de este már nem.
items.english: In the morning you can run in the park, but not in the evening anymore.

sections.content: már ("already, anymore") next to a negative changes the meaning slightly: nem lehet says something simply isn't possible, while már nem lehet says it used to be possible but the window has closed — useful for talking about opening hours and deadlines.
